html:
SMTO-LLM-0014 — Model response was interrupted

GUID: 89a12db4-722b-40e1-a14b-1f3058d225df
Slug: llm-stream-interrupted
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model's reply stopped partway through. SMTO didn't act on the unfinished part, and steps the task had already finished stay done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This quick test shows whether the model server is reachable and answering right now.
  2. If the check fails, make sure the computer or service running the model is switched on, hasn't restarted, and is reachable from your network. A reply breaks off when the model server stops, restarts or loses its connection in the middle of answering.
  3. When the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The unfinished reply was never acted on, so continuing is safe and finished steps are not repeated.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model's reply finishes without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it happened, to the person who manages the model server. If the reply always stops at about the same point, tell them that too.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model's streamed response ended or failed before a valid finish signal arrived, so no decision from it was accepted; a specific transport cause is shown only if one was recorded.

What this means

  • The current model response did not reach a trustworthy completion. If a more specific transport cause was retained it is shown separately; otherwise the reason remains unknown. A discarded decision does not undo earlier successful tools, and no-operation evidence applies only to this decision.

Why this can happen

  • The completion marker or complete response was not available. A transport interruption or provider failure remains possible until the recorded phase distinguishes it.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the last stream phase and any retained transport category. Compare the provider’s completion record for that request time with the interrupted response.

How to fix it

  • Check stream_failure_stage, time_to_first_event_seconds, stream_idle_seconds_at_failure and any retained category in provider_diagnostic, and compare with provider and proxy logs for restarts, idle timeouts or dropped connections. Fix that cause, then resume; earlier tool results and receipts remain recorded and are not replayed.
  • Check provider and connection health using the recorded stream phase. Keep earlier tool results and receipts when continuing the task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A subsequent model response reaches a valid completion without an interrupted-stream diagnostic.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Missing stream completion and broad stream wrappers do not prove a specific underlying cause; the no_operation_authorized fact is scoped to this decision.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
